_comment: CI wall-clock budgets for .github/workflows/ci.yml, enforced by the
'CI wall-clock budget' job via scripts/check_ci_wall_clock.py (issue
#1971). Budgets are in SECONDS and were derived from the measured
baseline recorded below -- see docs/guides/ci-wall-clock-budget.md for
the full per-job breakdown, the derivation, and how to re-measure.
These are regression budgets, NOT the hard ceilings that ci.yml's
per-job `timeout-minutes` already provides. A timeout only fires once a
job blows way past budget (the `test` matrix has a 45-minute ceiling on
a job whose median is 3 minutes); these budgets fire at roughly 2x the
measured p90, which is the band where a real regression lives and
ordinary runner noise does not.
Raising a budget is a legitimate change -- say why in the PR. Silently
raising it to make a red run green is the drift this file exists to stop.
'Golden artifacts (hash seed + path varied)' (issue #2225) is the one
row NOT derived from the baseline below -- that job did not exist when
the baseline was measured. 300s is a deliberately conservative first
estimate for two checkouts + one uv sync + ~1.5s of generators (still
half the 600s an unbudgeted job would inherit); re-derive it from real
timings at the next re-measure.
'Tests (numpy cross-check)' (issue #2276) gets the same treatment as
the row above, for the same reasons: it did not exist at measure time,
it is the same two-checkouts + one uv sync shape plus a ~2s pytest
suite, and 300s is a deliberately conservative first estimate --
re-derive it from real timings at the next re-measure rather than
trusting this guess.
total_job_budget_seconds is 1560, not the 1500 the pre-#2276 baseline
carried: the new numpy cross-check job is a permanent ~15s compute
addition (measured on its first PR run), and #2276 deliberately
duplicates the artifact-determinism drift detector inside it -- the
issue's point is that a drift detector must EXECUTE in the dep-full
environment, so that cost is load-bearing, not incidental. 60s of
headroom absorbs the new row with margin for runner noise; the next
baseline re-measure folds it into the derived numbers properly.

baseline.sample: the 25 most recent successful ci.yml runs
